gaps.sentence: Do not be ___ (PATIENT) with the trainees — everyone learns at a different pace.
gaps.explanation: 'Do not be impatient' — the negative adjective fits the advice against frustration.

gaps.sentence: His ___ (SHORT) of funds forced him to abandon the trip.
gaps.explanation: 'Shortage of funds' — the noun for an insufficient amount.

gaps.sentence: There's a growing ___ (AWARE) of mental health issues.

gaps.explanation: 'Applause' is the noun; 'applaud' is the verb.

gaps.sentence: The instructions have been ___ (SIMPLE) so that children can follow them.
gaps.explanation: Passive 'have been simplified' — the verb form meaning made simpler.

gaps.sentence: The mountain road has been ___ (WIDE) to cope with coach traffic.
gaps.explanation: Passive 'has been widened' — the verb form meaning made wider.

gaps.sentence: The ___ (ARRIVE) of the delegation was delayed by the storm.

gaps.explanation: 'Highly suspicious' — the adjective for something that looks wrong.
